correctness.rationale: The staggered gauge t_i=(−1)^i s_i is compatible with the periodic edge for even n and gives Δ_iH=2t_i[h−J(t_{i−1}+t_{i+1})]. For 0<h<2J the bracket is negative exactly when both neighbors are +1 and positive otherwise. Hence defects are independent and every aligned site has a defect neighbor: this is precisely a maximal independent subset of the labeled cycle. The interdefect distances are 2 or 3. For k defects exactly n−2k of the gaps are long, and marking a defect gives n times the binomial count with k-mark multiplicity, irrespective of rotational symmetry. The three-state gap automaton counts labeled closed paths, with characteristic polynomial x³−x−1 and initial traces 3,0,2. Its nonreal roots have common modulus ρ^(−1/2), yielding log ρ along the even lengths. At h=2J the energy is −nJ+4J times the number of adjacent defect pairs, so all independent sets are ground states and the Lucas comparison is correct; the domination condition is lost. A separately written exact physical-flip census at J=1,h=3/4 tested every spin assignment for n=4,6,…,18, the individual stability equivalence, and every k coefficient; totals were 2,5,10,17,29,51,90,158. value.rationale: The model's local-minimum census is a meaningful observable, but this frozen result reproduces an existing weighted partition after taking a hub sector and changing a field without changing any local flip sign. It adds neither a new stability mechanism nor a different counting problem; the endpoint comparison is already known and the only leftover size is elementary. As a standalone contribution it is a routine specialization rather than a new useful exact invariant.
